summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with unresectable extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma and recent history of GNR bacteremia and C. difficile infection, was admitted with a two-week cough, two days of fatigue, and a one-day history of low-grade fever up to 101°F. He was evaluated for possible cholangitis given his elevated bilirubin and history of biliary stents. CT imaging suggested partial obstruction of the left biliary stent, but he defervesced without intervention, and liver tests normalized. Blood cultures remained negative at 72 hours, respiratory viral panel was negative, and no evidence of colitis was found. His leukopenia and thrombocytopenia were likely due to chemotherapy or a viral illness. He improved clinically and was discharged home with instructions to follow up with oncology for CBC monitoring and ongoing cancer care.
